newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa's bonds continued to gyrate at weaker levels during thin late Monday trade as players trying to pick value encountered scattered selling around key support levels.
At 1405 GMT the benchmark R150 long bond stood at 14.965 from Friday's late level of 14.915, the yield having spiked toward the key psychological level of 15.00 pct four times over the day.
"I think 14.97-98 has become a bit of a level. It did bump off there on Friday," said one dealer.
The dealer added that some players were still fishing for stock around 15.00-05 but seemed happy to wear a six to seven-point premium for the time being.

In currency dealings, the spot rand was at 4.4605/4635 against a weak dollar, a tad stronger than 4.4620/4650 late Friday. Traders said the unit had bobbed around in a narrow range of 4.4630-4.4590 amid steady but uninspiring two-way flows.
"We're so range-bound its scary," remarked one dealer.

Against the crosses the rand's fortunes see-sawed with a morning push lower against the mark parried by an afternoon recovery in the U.S. dollar against the German currency which sent the local currency to 0.3813/3816 from 0.3794/3797 on Friday.

The Japanese yen, however, kept the upper hand throughout the day, and the rand was last at 26.5965/6256 yen from 27.2350/2946 previously. Against sterling the rand was at 7.2394/2487, weakening from its late Friday level of 7.2203/2296.

Bond and currency players said their markets were likely to brush off March producer price inflation figures which were forecast to show a 0.4 percentage point year-on-year rise when released on Thursday.
